newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT, RUGBY UNION-Defence first and foremost, says Endacott.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT, RUGBY UNION-Defence first and foremost, says Endacott.

text.p: AUCKLAND, July 30 - Auckland Warriors coach Frank Endacott will this week stress the need for a strong defence ahead of his team's World Club Championship rugby league match against Warrington in Christchurch, NZPA reports.
The Warriors are heavy favourites in their final preliminary round match at Lancaster Park on Sunday.
Warrington arrive in Christchurch following their fifth loss, 0-44, to Cronulla last weekend.
"The problem with those teams is that you might go into a game thinking you're hot and get all cocky," Endacott said.
"But it's not unheard of in sport for huge upsets and if you give those kinds of teams a sniff and a chance they'll be at your throat."
Endacott said he would impress the need to concentrate on the basics this week.
"I will be mentioning the need for a good points differential from this final game to get ahead of Brisbane, who will be playing Halifax on Monday after our game," Endacott said.
"We want to top the table so that we get a home draw in both the quarterfinal and semifinal, assuming we win through and end up playing Brisbane.
"But before all of that, first and foremost we have to think about a win, even by one point, then playing well, and finally trying to put as many points on them as we can in that order."
The Warriors coach, whose team thrashed British leaders Bradford 64-14 and Challenge Cup champions St Helens 70-6 in Auckland, says the key attribute this weekend will be defence.
"There are no two ways about it. If we defend well everything else will fall into place," he said.
"If we defend well it means we are concentrating. If we are concentrating then we can pick up our game where we left off last week and if that happens then everything should fall into place."
Auckland and Brisbane are tied at the top of the most competitive section of the tournament, Australasia A, on a joint points differential of plus 174.
Endacott is today likely to confirm the same squad of 17 which beat St Helens last weekend.
